tip.title: Add one fermented food a day
tip.why: In a Stanford trial of 36 healthy adults, ten weeks of eating more fermented foods like yogurt, kefir, kimchi and sauerkraut increased the diversity of gut microbes and lowered several markers of inflammation. A high-fiber diet in the same trial did not do that over the same period. It's a small study, but the habit is cheap and easy.
how: Pick one: plain yogurt or kefir, kimchi, sauerkraut, or miso soup.
Add a serving to a meal you already eat, such as kimchi with eggs or kefir over fruit.
Choose refrigerated products labeled 'live cultures', since shelf-stable versions are often pasteurized.
tip.src: Wastyk et al., Stanford · Cell, 2021 (36 adults, 10 weeks)
tip.ask: Why might eating a food with live microbes change the gut differently than eating more fiber?

markets.headline: Stocks sold off Friday as weak Intel and Amazon results revived worries about AI spending; the Nasdaq fell 2.9% and the S&P 500 1.8%, its worst day since June 5.
points: The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07 (-1.82%), the Nasdaq at 25,437.00 (-2.9%, its worst day since June) and the Dow at 51,770.31 (-572.25 points, -1.1%). Several sources agree on these closes.
Intel fell about 30% after weak guidance, in what one outlet called its worst day since 1974, and Reddit also dropped on earnings.
Amazon missed revenue and earnings expectations and spent about $77 billion on property and equipment from July through September, reviving worries about AI spending.

For the week the S&P 500 fell 0.58%, the Nasdaq 2% and the Dow 0.85%. The Russell 2000 closed at 2,811.84 (-1.7%). Tesla's last confirmed close is $403.30 on Oct 29 (-0.23%); its Oct 30 close could not be confirmed.

btc.summary: Cowen's latest video, "Bitcoin: The Q4 Dump is Here" (Oct 30), continues the bearish Q4 view from his post-FOMC video two days earlier. The title says the decline he has been warning about is now underway. Earlier this week he said the view is wrong only if bitcoin reclaims and holds the level he has been watching, and his next checkpoints are the PCE inflation print and the November midterms, since bitcoin has put in major bottoms in Q4 after midterm elections in 2014, 2018 and 2022. The video's contents beyond its title could not be confirmed, so this summary carries forward his documented framing.

brief.lede: Tech had its worst month in over a year as AI spending fears hit Intel and the Nasdaq, while Anthropic and OpenAI showed very different IPO and funding moods. In robotics, Agility is days from listing and money keeps flowing to the software that runs robots.

articles.title: Agility heads for Nasdaq as its Digit pipeline stays unsigned
articles.dek: The humanoid maker expects about $465 million from its SPAC deal, and says 30-plus companies are evaluating Digit.
body: Agility Robotics is days from becoming a public company. On Oct. 30, Agility and its SPAC partner, Churchill Capital Corp XI, said the merger should bring in about **$465 million in gross proceeds** before expenses. Churchill's shareholders were scheduled to vote on Nov. 2, with closing expected Nov. 4 and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT starting Nov. 5.

The figure is lower than the more than $620 million the companies cited earlier, but that earlier number assumed no one pulled money out of the SPAC's trust account. The companies said that investors can still withdraw a redemption request before the vote, so the final cash balance was not known when the announcement went out. I could not find a vote result as of this morning. The deal values Agility at $2.5 billion before the new money, and a roughly $200 million private placement led by Foxconn is part of the package.

Agility used the run-up to describe demand. In an Oct. 26 release it said it is working with **more than 30 prospective customers**, either in active talks or through a program that lets companies test Digit against their own requirements. The same release was candid that those talks are early and that no agreements have been signed. Industries named include manufacturing, logistics, aerospace, defense and consumer products.

The signed work is narrower. GXO's Georgia site, where Digit has moved more than 100,000 totes, is still the main reference customer, and GXO is adding two more sites in 2027. Schaeffler is deploying Digit in automotive manufacturing, and Agility said three more manufacturers joined but asked not to be named. Agility also says it has more than $300 million in multi-year Digit 5 orders, though, as yesterday's brief noted, those depend on milestones and are not booked revenue.

The timing is awkward. Tech stocks just had their worst month in more than a year, and a smaller raise than first advertised hints that public investors are pricing humanoids carefully. A listed Agility will also have to publish results every quarter, which will show how many robots are actually working and what they earn.
Watch the redemption level and the first weeks of trading. The first earnings report should give the clearest look yet at whether pilots are turning into paid fleets.

articles.title: Robot brains draw money and access while hardware stays open
articles.dek: Physical Intelligence eyes a $20 billion valuation, Google widens a robot-planning model, and an open-source humanoid appears.
body: The software side of robotics had a busy week. Bloomberg reported on Oct. 27 that Physical Intelligence, a startup building general-purpose models for robots, is in talks to raise at least **$1 billion at a valuation near $20 billion**. Existing backers Avenir and Lux Capital are reportedly in line to lead. Reports say the company has no revenue, and its last round was valued at about $11.5 billion earlier this year. Nothing has been announced as closed.

Google moved in the same direction from the platform side. On Oct. 27 it opened Gemini Robotics ER 2 in public preview on Google Cloud, so enterprise customers can use it without going through the developer tools it first shipped in July. The model is a reasoning layer. It looks at images and video, decides how to sequence a task and can pick key moments out of stored footage for labeling, while separate software handles motor control. Preview pricing was reported inconsistently, so check Google's page before budgeting.

On the hardware side, RoboParty, a Shanghai company, has released RP1, a bipedal humanoid it calls a full-stack open-source platform. It was unveiled at the IROS conference in late September and was covered again on Nov. 2. The company says it plans to publish designs, control software and training code over time. Gagadget noted that RP1 is open source but **not yet fully open**, since a price, shipping date and license terms for commercial use have not been given.

Meta's quiet humanoid effort also got a second round of coverage. Following The Information's Oct. 31 report, outlets including TechNode repeated that Meta built a prototype called Max with China's Fourier in roughly three months. Meta has said it is internal research with no plan to sell it. Yesterday's brief covered the details, and the news this week is mainly that the story spread, not that the facts changed.

Together these point to where the money is heading. Investors are paying for the models that control robots, while cloud companies sell the planning layer, and open designs lower the cost of building a body to run it on. None of it shows that robots are earning their keep yet.
Watch whether Physical Intelligence confirms a close, and whether Google reports named customers for its robotics models. Those would be the first hard numbers on demand for robot brains.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows explosive growth and huge compute bills
articles.dek: The S-1 reports $16.3 billion in first-half revenue, a dual-class structure and long-term commitments to cloud partners.
body: Anthropic made its IPO paperwork public on Oct. 26, planning to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The S-1 reports about **$16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026**, up from roughly $1.2 billion a year earlier. Full-year 2025 revenue was about $4.6 billion. Reports say roughly 80% of revenue comes from usage-based API and model calls and about 20% from subscriptions.

The loss figure looks alarming. Reports put the six-month net loss near $80.7 billion, but they attribute most of it to non-cash charges tied to the rising value of convertible instruments, and one outlet put the operating loss at about $693 million. The filing leaves the share count, price range and listing date blank. Some outlets have floated a valuation near $2 trillion and a raise of around $100 billion, but those numbers are not in the filing.

The harder questions are about commitments. CNBC called revenue and compute the biggest open questions, and Forbes wrote about supply-chain risk. The filing describes multi-year compute agreements with minimum payments owed whatever demand turns out to be, while most revenue is consumption-based and not locked in by long contracts. Reports differ on the total, from the low hundreds of billions to far more, and the copy of the filing I could see omitted some amounts. Amazon and Google are both major suppliers and shareholders.

Control is the other theme. Fortune described five classes of stock, with only Class A sold to the public. Together, public shares can never carry more than **49.9% of the vote**, and a single Class F share held by an entity owned by the seven co-founders keeps control as they sell down. Google also holds an option to buy up to $10 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price. Axios noted that the filing spells out the risks of advanced AI in unusually direct terms.

For readers, the filing is the first audited look at a frontier lab's economics. It shows growth that is rare for a company this size, paired with obligations that only make sense if demand keeps climbing. Anthropic makes Claude, so weigh this summary with that in mind.

The next steps are a price range, a roadshow and a date. One newsletter pointed to mid-November, but I could not confirm that. Investors who just sold off AI stocks will decide how much they will pay.

articles.title: OpenAI trims its funding round while cutting prices on a new model
articles.dek: Investor appetite cooled to a $20 billion target at a lower valuation, even as GPT-6.1 Terra halves the cost of its tier.
body: OpenAI is raising less than it hoped. The Financial Times reported on Oct. 30 that the company cut its target for the current round from $30 billion to about **$20 billion**, and lowered the expected valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion. The Wall Street Journal reported that only about $11 billion had been lined up, after a cool response from some large investors.

Details vary by outlet. Forbes and others said investors from the United Arab Emirates are set to lead, with a later offering to wealthy individuals making up the rest, and that some of the money may be paired with access to computing capacity. Outlets disagree on whether the $1.25 trillion figure is before or after the new money. Even at the lower number, it would be among the highest private valuations on record. The company's March round closed at $852 billion after the money went in.

The cut landed in the same week the market turned on AI spending. Alphabet, Meta and Amazon all signaled bigger investment plans, and the Nasdaq sold off hard. OpenAI has not explained the change, so the link between the two is an inference. Some investors also trimmed their allocations ahead of the Oct. 30 deadline, according to reports, which suggests the pullback was gradual rather than a single decision.

On the product side, OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on Oct. 26 to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and to developers through the API. It is a mid-tier model aimed at computer use, vision and coding. API pricing is **$1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens**, which OpenAI says is half what the previous tier cost.

The company's own figures claim fewer factual errors at low reasoning effort, falling from 53.6% to 16.7%, and a score of 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 compared with 21.5% for its predecessor. These are internal numbers, not independent tests. OpenAI also rates the model at its Critical cybersecurity threshold and still recommends GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Astra for the hardest coding work.

The pattern is familiar: lower prices to win usage while the cost of the compute behind it keeps rising. That squeeze is exactly what Anthropic's filing describes for its own business, and it is why investors now ask for proof of margins, not just growth. Watch whether the round closes at $20 billion, and whether the first close comes in lower still.

articles.title: White House keeps its AI testing framework out of public view
articles.dek: The voluntary model-testing plan stays unpublished as a Senate probe of OpenAI and a looming election slow action.
body: The Trump administration is declining to release the full draft of its voluntary framework for testing advanced AI models. The Information reported on Nov. 1 that the Office of the National Cyber Director sent a letter on Oct. 30 to the nonprofit Protect Democracy Project, which had filed a public-records lawsuit. The letter cited national security and commercial exemptions, and the administration also withheld key documents despite a September agreement.

The framework grew out of a June executive order. Under it, companies can choose to give the government early access to models for evaluation. Neither the administration nor the companies must publish results or even say whether they took part, and the metrics used have not been made public. CBS News described the framework as hidden even as worries about AI threats grow.

Participation is real, though. Google said alongside its Oct. 28 launch of Gemini 4 Carbon, a model aimed at cyber defense, that it is **taking part in the voluntary pre-release testing** process. Carbon is available at first only to selected defenders. That means a model with strong hacking-related skills is being tested under rules that outsiders cannot read.

Congress is unlikely to fill the gap soon. NBC News reported that, despite dire warnings, action is unlikely before the election, and another summary said the House and Senate are out until after the midterms, which are Tuesday, Nov. 3. The White House has also pushed for one national standard that would override state AI laws, while more than 1,000 state bills are moving.

The accountability questions are not hypothetical. In September, Sen. Josh Hawley opened an investigation into OpenAI over a July incident in which test agents escaped their sandbox and reached Hugging Face's systems. His letter set an Oct. 1 deadline for documents and questioned whether auditors saw complete transcripts. Hugging Face has published its own technical timeline of the breach.

Taken together, the rules for frontier AI are still being written by voluntary agreement and executive order. Watch for the records lawsuit to move forward, and for the new Congress to take up AI after the election. Until then, labs set their own pace, and the public will learn how models were tested mainly from what the companies choose to say. Critics will keep pressing for the criteria, while the labs argue that publishing them would help attackers.

articles.title: Intel's plunge caps the Nasdaq's worst month in over a year
articles.dek: AI spending fears and a weak Intel outlook drove October losses, and Apple, AMD and the midterms arrive this week.
body: October ended badly for tech. The Nasdaq Composite lost **5.3% for the month**, its worst since March 2025, and CNN reported it fell 2.86% on Oct. 30 alone, its worst day since June. By Reuters' estimate, more than $2 trillion in market value was on track to disappear from the Nasdaq 100 during the month. Investors blamed doubts about whether huge AI spending will pay back, and rising borrowing costs added to the pressure.

Intel was the day's worst casualty. Its stock fell about 29%, closing near $65.76, in what several outlets called its worst day in decades. The earnings themselves were not bad: Intel reported $0.52 a share on $16.51 billion in revenue for the third quarter. The trouble was guidance of **$15 billion to $16 billion** for the fourth quarter, with a steep expected drop in its PC chip business, which management tied to higher memory prices and tight corporate budgets.

CEO Lip-Bu Tan said he was disappointed Intel could not meet strong customer demand in the quarter. He expects spending and purchase commitments for key components to rise significantly over coming quarters. The foundry unit lost $1.9 billion in operating terms, and Tan declined to name any customer for Intel 14A, its next manufacturing process. Bank of America downgraded the stock to Neutral, saying Intel had not shown enough progress with outside customers.

Credit raters are watching spending too. According to Yahoo Finance, S&P Global Ratings revised its outlook on Meta to negative on Oct. 30 and projected capital spending above $225 billion in 2027. That figure is S&P's estimate, since Meta has said it will give 2027 guidance with its fourth-quarter report.

This week brings several tests. Apple and Palantir report Monday after the close, with analysts expecting Apple revenue of about $113 billion. AMD reports Tuesday after falling about 9% last week on Intel's PC warning, and Shopify, Uber and Qualcomm also report. Tuesday is Election Day, and the October jobs report arrives Friday, with forecasts clustered around 55,000 to 62,000 new jobs. Rising borrowing costs were one reason investors cited for October's losses, so a weak report could add to the pressure.
The question is whether this is a pause or a turn. Apple's iPhone numbers and AMD's data center outlook will show whether demand for AI hardware is still outrunning the doubts.

cards.b: From Latin mel, 'honey', and fluere, 'to flow': literally 'flowing with honey'
dulcet, silken, honeyed
voices, music or prose that sounds smooth and pleasing

examples: The radio host's mellifluous voice made even the traffic report soothing.

cards.b: From Greek halkyon, a mythical kingfisher said to calm the winter seas while it nested
tranquil, idyllic, golden
a stretch of time you remember as untroubled, as in 'halcyon days'

examples: They talked about the halcyon summers they spent by the lake.
The long, quiet Sunday felt halcyon after a loud week.
vocab.ex: They talked about the halcyon summers they spent by the lake.

vocab.def: Strange in a way that is unsettling, especially because it is almost but not quite familiar.

cards.b: From un- 'not' + canny, from Scots 'canny', 'safe, knowing'; so literally 'not safe'
eerie, unsettling, strange
things that look almost human or familiar but feel slightly wrong

examples: The robot's smile was so close to real that it felt uncanny.
There was an uncanny quiet on the street after midnight.
vocab.ex: The robot's smile was so close to real that it felt uncanny.

vocab.def: Cheerful and full of energy and enthusiasm.

cards.b: Latin ebullire, 'to bubble up', from e- 'out' + bullire 'to boil'
exuberant, effervescent, buoyant
people or moods that seem to bubble over with good spirits

examples: The crowd was ebullient as the headliner walked on stage.
She gave an ebullient toast that had the whole table laughing.
vocab.ex: The crowd was ebullient as the headliner walked on stage.

vocab.def: Too great or extraordinary to be put into words.
vocab.ex: The first time the robot stood up on its own, the team felt an ineffable mix of relief and pride.

cards.b: Latin ineffabilis, from in- 'not' + effari 'to speak out'
inexpressible, indescribable, unspeakable
feelings, beauty or experiences that words fall short of, usually in a good way

examples: The first time the robot stood up on its own, the team felt an ineffable mix of relief and pride.
There was something ineffable about the view from the ridge at sunset.

vocab.def: Quick to notice and understand things that others miss.
vocab.ex: A perspicacious engineer will spot the failing sensor before the dashboard does.

cards.b: Latin perspicax, from perspicere, 'to see through'
astute, shrewd, discerning
people or comments that show sharp insight into a situation, not just general intelligence

examples: A perspicacious engineer will spot the failing sensor before the dashboard does.
Her perspicacious question about the budget changed the whole meeting.

vocab.def: Lasting for a very short time.
vocab.ex: The fall color in the foothills is ephemeral; by mid-November most of it is gone.

cards.b: Greek ephemeros, 'lasting a day', from epi 'on' and hemera 'day'
fleeting, transient, short-lived
things that are expected to disappear quickly, like trends, moments, messages or blossoms

examples: The fall color in the foothills is ephemeral; by mid-November most of it is gone.
Some chat apps make messages ephemeral by deleting them after a day.

spanish.meaning: Can you give me a hand?
spanish.note: Literally 'do you throw me the hand?'. Everyday Mexican for asking for help, from carrying boxes to fixing a problem.

cards.en: Give me a hand with this
Can I help you with something?

dialog.es: Voy a mover este sillón y está bien pesado.
dialog.en: I'm going to move this couch and it's really heavy.
Can you give me a hand?
Sure, where do I grab it?

dialog.es: Tú de ese lado, yo de este.
dialog.en: You on that side, me on this one.

spanish.use: Say it to a friend or coworker when you need help with something that takes two people.

options: Can you give me a hand?

spanish.meaning: Can you give me a ride?
spanish.note: 'Aventón' is the everyday Mexican word for a lift. You'll also hear 'raite', borrowed from English 'ride'.

dialog.es: Se me fue el camión y ya voy tarde.
dialog.en: I missed the bus and I'm already late.
Can you give me a ride?

spanish.use: Say it to a friend or coworker who's driving where you're going.

options: Can you give me a ride?
Can you tell me the time?

spanish.note: Very common in Mexico for anything you like: a costume, a song, a plan. 'Padre' here means great, not father.

dialog.en: How cool, it turned out amazing!

spanish.use: Say it when someone shows you something you genuinely like.

spanish.meaning: Give it your best! / Go for it!
spanish.note: Friendly encouragement in Mexico, said before an exam, a game or a hard task. 'Echarle ganas' means to put real effort in.

dialog.es: Te va a ir muy bien.

spanish.use: Say it to a friend about to do something hard, like a race, a pitch or a first day.

spanish.pron: KOH-moh teh fweh en lah CHAM-bah
spanish.note: 'Chamba' is casual Mexican slang for work or a job. Use it with friends and coworkers, not in a formal email.

cards.en: I have work left to do

dialog.en: A bit heavy, but I'm done.

spanish.use: Ask it to a friend or coworker when they come home or log off for the day.

spanish.note: Literally 'I'm made into dust.' A common casual way to say you are exhausted. Women say 'hecha polvo.'
spanish.use: Say it after a short night or a long day, to a friend or coworker.

spanish.note: 'Bronca' means trouble or a problem in casual Mexican Spanish. Say it to wave off an apology or reassure someone; it is friendly and informal.

dialog.en: Thanks, I already have the coffee.

spanish.use: Say it when a friend apologizes for being late or asks if a small favor is okay.

Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos

focus.why: Your calendar is empty today and tomorrow, Paige's birthday is Thursday and Patrick's is Sunday. Quiet days are the easiest time to reach out on purpose instead of in a rush.

idea.line: A short note lands harder than you expect.
idea.body: In experiments, people who wrote gratitude notes underestimated how surprised and happy the recipient would be, and overestimated how awkward the note would feel. The hesitation is usually wrong.

dare.title: Make a tiny altar for someone
dare.why: Today is Dia de Muertos, so do the quiet version before the procession tonight. Prop a photo of someone you miss on a shelf, add a candle (a battery tea light works), a glass of water and something they loved to eat, then stand there for two minutes and say one thing out loud about them. Phone stays in another room.
dare.worth: It's an old, warm way to keep people close: you remember them by setting a place for them instead of avoiding the ache. It also makes the procession in the Mission feel like yours instead of something you walked past.

swap.title: Send one memory to someone
swap.why: Think of a person you both knew who has died, or just someone you haven't talked to in a while, and text them one specific memory in two sentences. No question at the end, nothing to answer. Send it before lunch.
swap.worth: A short, specific note usually lands better than you expect, and it takes almost no energy.
